And Mary herself tells us the secret of her greatness in the Magnificat: “He has looked with favour on the lowliness of his servant… the Mighty One has done great things for me.” Not pride, but gratitude. Everything is God's mercy.

What God did in Mary at the beginning, he wants to do in us at the end: to make us holy and blameless before him in love. So in this season, let us prepare a clean heart for Jesus by a good confession. Holy Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to you. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary was kept free from every sin by God from the very first moment of her life. Ask Mary to help you keep your heart clean and full of love for Jesus!

opts.a: Mary, the new Eve and the Ark of the Covenant
intro: The Fathers of the Church loved to read the Old Testament with Mary in mind. Two images help us understand this feast: the new Eve and the Ark.

sub: Eve listened to the serpent; Mary listened to the angel.
Eve's disobedience brought death; Mary's obedience opened the way to life.
St Irenaeus: the knot of Eve was untied by Mary.
points.apply: When tempted, say Mary's words: let it be done according to your word.

sub: The Ark held the tablets, the manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4).
Mary carried the Word, the Bread of Life, the eternal Priest.
The Ark was made pure; Mary was preserved from all stain.
points.apply: Receive Christ in the Holy Qurbana with a clean heart, like Mary.

sub: God prepared a pure dwelling for His Son.
Mary was redeemed in a more exalted way.
What God did for her, He wants to begin in us.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Christmas.

concl: Mary Immaculate shows us what grace can do and what we are called to be.
The feast in Advent prepares a clean dwelling for Christ in us.
opts.resolve: Before Christmas I will make a good confession to prepare a clean dwelling for Christ.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the early Christians did not have the dogma of the Immaculate Conception in its later words, but they had a deep intuition about Mary, drawn from the Scriptures. Let us look at two images that the Fathers loved: Mary as the new Eve, and Mary as the Ark of the Covenant.

In the garden, Eve listened to the serpent and believed his lie. Through her disobedience, sin and death entered the world. But God promised that the offspring of a woman would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). In Nazareth another woman listened, not to a serpent but to an angel, and said: here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). St Irenaeus wrote that the knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience. Where Eve said no, Mary said yes.

The second image is the Ark of the Covenant. God commanded Moses to make it of acacia wood, covered with pure gold inside and out (Exodus 25:10–11). Inside were the tablets of the law, a jar of manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4). When the Ark entered a house, it brought blessing; David danced before it. Mary carried in her womb the Word of God, the true Bread from heaven and the eternal High Priest. When she entered Elizabeth's house, the child leaped for joy (Luke 1:41). If the Ark had to be pure gold, how much more the living Ark of the Son of God.

This is what the Church proclaims today: that from the first moment of her conception Mary was preserved from every stain of original sin, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ. She too was saved by her Son, but in a more exalted way: preserved rather than cleansed.

And what God did perfectly for Mary, He wants to begin in us. In Baptism we were washed; in confession we are cleansed again; in the Holy Qurbana we receive Christ as Mary did. This Advent, let us prepare a clean dwelling for Him. Make a good confession before Christmas, and ask Mary Immaculate to teach you to say yes.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the dogma of the Immaculate Conception
intro: Many people confuse this feast with the virginal conception of Jesus. Let us be clear about what the Church teaches and why.

sub: Defined by Pope Pius IX in 1854 (Ineffabilis Deus).
Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception (CCC 491).
By a singular grace, in view of the merits of Christ.
points.apply: Learn the difference between the Immaculate Conception and the Virgin Birth.

sub: The angel's greeting: kecharitomene, highly favoured, filled with grace (Luke 1:28).
Mary was redeemed by her Son (CCC 492).
She remained free of personal sin all her life (CCC 493).
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly, attentive to the words full of grace.

points.h: Lourdes and the faith of the people
sub: 1858: I am the Immaculate Conception.
Eastern tradition: Mary the All-Holy, Panagia (CCC 493).
Our own Churches' devotion to Mary.
points.apply: Honour Mary this Advent with the Rosary.

concl: The dogma honours Christ, whose grace made Mary all-holy.
Mary Immaculate is the model and mother of the Church.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray the Rosary and ask Mary to make my heart pure.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, many Catholics think that today's feast is about the conception of Jesus in Mary's womb. It is not. That we celebrate on 25 March, the Annunciation. Today we celebrate the conception of Mary herself in the womb of her mother, whom tradition names Anne.

On 8 December 1854, Pope Pius IX solemnly defined that the most Blessed Virgin Mary, from the first moment of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege of almighty God, and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ the Saviour of the human race, was preserved free from all stain of original sin (CCC 491). Every word matters. Singular grace: it was God's gift, not Mary's achievement. In view of the merits of Jesus Christ: Mary too was saved by her Son.

Where is this in the Bible? The angel greets Mary as full of grace (Luke 1:28). The Greek word means one who has been, and remains, filled with God's favour. The Church understood that the woman chosen to be the Mother of God was prepared by grace from the beginning. The Catechism says that Mary was redeemed from the moment of her conception, and that by God's grace she remained free of every personal sin her whole life long (CCC 492–493). The Eastern Fathers call her Panagia, the All-Holy.

Four years after the definition, in 1858, Our Lady appeared to a poor girl, Bernadette, at Lourdes. When Bernadette asked her name, she answered: I am the Immaculate Conception. Bernadette did not understand the words, but the parish priest did. Heaven confirmed what the Church had taught.

Why does this matter? Because it shows what God's grace can do. Mary is not a goddess; she is a creature, entirely filled with grace. She shows what the Church is called to become: holy and without blemish (Ephesians 5:27). So let us honour her this Advent with the Rosary, and ask her to help us prepare for her Son at this Holy Qurbana and at Christmas.

Dear friends, the day after Christmas the Church remembers St Stephen, the first martyr. It seems abrupt: from the crib to stones. But the Fathers saw the connection: yesterday Christ was born on earth, so that today Stephen might be born into heaven.

Stephen was full of grace and power and of the Holy Spirit. His opponents could not withstand his wisdom. When they stoned him, he saw the heavens opened and Jesus standing at the right hand of God (Acts 6:8–10; 7:55–56).
As he died, he prayed: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit; and kneeling, he cried out: Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:59–60). He died like his Master, forgiving.

Jesus warned that His disciples would be hated for His name, but whoever endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 10:22). Let us pray for persecuted Christians, and let us forgive someone this Christmas, as Stephen did. Amen.
kids: Children, St Stephen loved Jesus so much that he forgave the people who hurt him. Can you forgive someone today?

homily: Dear friends, today our Church keeps Holy Childhood Day, remembering the Holy Innocents. The joy of Christmas is followed by tears in Bethlehem: Herod kills the little boys, and Rachel weeps for her children (Matthew 2:16–18).

From Abel onward, innocent blood has cried out to God (Genesis 4:10). The Letter to the Hebrews remembers those who suffered for their faith, of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38). God hears every innocent cry.
Today let us think of children who suffer: the unborn, the abused, the hungry, child workers, refugee children. Jesus Himself became a refugee child, fleeing to Egypt.

On Holy Childhood Day, children help children: through prayer and small offerings, they support missions for poor children around the world. Parents, encourage your children in this. And let us all protect the little ones God entrusts to us. Amen.
kids: Children, today is your special day! Pray for children who are sad, hungry or in danger, and share something to help them.

homily: Dear friends, today the twenty-five-day fast before Christmas begins in our Church, and St Paul gives the right call: now is the moment to wake from sleep; the night is far gone, the day is near; let us lay aside the works of darkness and put on the armour of light (Romans 13:11–12). The fast is a waking up.
Paul is very concrete: no drunkenness, no quarrelling, no jealousy; instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 13:13–14). Fasting from food helps us fast from sin.

In the Gospel the angel tells Zechariah that his prayer has been heard, but Zechariah does not believe, and he becomes unable to speak until the promise is fulfilled (Luke 1:18–20). His silence was a discipline, but also a gift: nine months to listen to God.

Let our fast this year include some silence: less phone, less television, less gossip, more prayer and more listening to God's word. Then, like Zechariah, we will have a song ready at Christmas. Amen.
kids: Children, the fast before Christmas is like waking up early to get ready for a big feast. Give up one small thing for Jesus this month!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul thanks God for the gifts given to the Corinthians as they wait for the coming of the Lord, and assures them: God is faithful; by Him you were called into the fellowship of His Son (1 Corinthians 1:9). The whole season of Annunciation rests on God's faithfulness: what He promises, He does.
In the Gospel Jesus says: the one who sent me is with me; He has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to Him (John 8:29). Jesus lives in constant communion with the Father.
This is a great comfort. Because Jesus was never alone, we who belong to Him are never alone either. Even in loneliness, illness or exile, the Father is with us.
The secret Jesus gives is simple: I always do what is pleasing to Him. During this fast, let us ask each evening: did I do today what pleases the Father? Then we too will know His presence. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: my Father is always with me. God is always with you too, even when you feel alone!

homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate St Francis Xavier, who preached along the southern coasts of India, including Travancore, more than four hundred and eighty years ago. Isaiah calls: turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth (Isaiah 45:22). Francis brought that call to our shores.

St Paul describes the life of an apostle: in hardships, sleepless nights and hunger; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:4–10). Francis lived exactly so: tired, poor, yet rich in God.

In the Gospel Jesus sends out the Twelve with nothing for the journey except a staff: no bread, no bag, no money (Mark 6:8). They must trust God and the hospitality of the people. And they preached repentance, cast out demons and healed the sick.
We are heirs of missionaries. Let us thank God for those who brought and kept the faith in India, pray for missionaries today, and share the Gospel in our own surroundings, simply and with joy. Amen.
kids: Children, St Francis Xavier taught children prayers with songs. Sing a prayer song today and teach it to a friend!

homily: Dear friends, on this First Friday St Paul tells us: if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is (Colossians 3:1). Our hearts are made for heaven, not only for earth.

Paul tells us to put to death what is earthly in us: impurity, greed, anger, lying; and to put on the new self, which is being renewed in the image of its Creator (Colossians 3:5–10). The fast is the time to change our clothes.

In the Gospel Jesus says to His disciples: blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear; many prophets longed to see what you see and did not see it (Matthew 13:16–17). We have the Gospel, the sacraments, the Holy Qurbana: gifts the prophets only dreamed of.
On this First Friday, honour the Sacred Heart of Jesus with a good confession and Holy Communion. Ask Him for eyes that truly see and ears that truly hear. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: happy are your eyes, because you can know me! Thank Jesus today that you know Him.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul asks the Galatians: did you receive the Spirit by doing the works of the law, or by believing what you heard? And he reminds them that those who believe are the children of Abraham (Galatians 3:2, 7). Faith is the open hand that receives God's gift.

In the Gospel three people want to follow Jesus. To one He says: foxes have holes, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head. To another who wants to bury his father first: let the dead bury their own dead. To a third who wants to say goodbye: no one who puts a hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God (Luke 9:57–62).
These are hard words. Jesus is not against family; He is against delay. When God calls, the answer must not be someday.
What is God asking you to do that you keep postponing? Reconciliation, confession, prayer, a change of habit? During this fast, put your hand to the plough and do not look back. Amen.
kids: Children, a farmer who looks back cannot plough a straight line. When Jesus asks you to do something good, do it right away!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul hopes that all of us may come to the unity of the faith and to maturity, the full stature of Christ, no longer children tossed to and fro by every wind of teaching, but speaking the truth in love and growing up in every way into Christ (Ephesians 4:13–15).

In the Gospel Jesus promises: whoever believes in me will do the works that I do and even greater works; if in my name you ask me for anything, I will do it (John 14:12–14). Prayer in the name of Jesus is prayer according to His heart.
Today we remember St Ambrose, the bishop of Milan, who was famous for speaking the truth in love. He baptised St Augustine, and he was brave enough to correct even the emperor when he sinned.
Let us ask for a mature faith: not shaken by every opinion on social media, but rooted in Christ and His Church. And let us speak the truth always with love. Amen.
kids: Children, St Ambrose helped a young man named Augustine to love Jesus. Pray today for a friend who needs Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul blesses God who chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before Him in love (Ephesians 1:4). Before we were born, God had a plan for each of us.

In the Gospel Mary asks the angel: how can this be, since I am a virgin? It is not doubt but a request for understanding. The angel explains that the Holy Spirit will come upon her, and adds: nothing will be impossible with God (Luke 1:34–37).
Mary then gives the answer that changed history: here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). God's plan for her became real through her yes.
God has a plan for you too. It may seem impossible, but nothing is impossible with God. Ask questions in prayer like Mary, and then give your yes. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary said yes to God. You can say yes to God every day by being kind and obedient!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul gives a list of Christian love: let love be genuine; love one another with mutual affection; outdo one another in showing honour; rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep (Romans 12:9–15).
In the Gospel Mary, having received the Word, does not stay at home. She goes with haste to the hill country to serve her elderly cousin Elizabeth (Luke 1:39). Love makes us hurry to help.

When Elizabeth hears Mary's greeting, the child John leaps in her womb, and she is filled with the Holy Spirit. She cries out: blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfilment of what was spoken to her by the Lord (Luke 1:41–45).

Mary carried Jesus to Elizabeth's house, and joy filled it. During this fast, let us visit someone who needs company: an elderly relative, a sick neighbour, a new mother. We too can carry Jesus to them. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary hurried to help her cousin. Who can you help at home today without being asked?

homily: Dear friends, St Paul asks the Corinthians to complete their collection for the poor of Jerusalem: it is a question of a fair balance; your abundance should supply their need (2 Corinthians 8:13–14). Fasting without sharing is only a diet.

In the Gospel Mary sings the Magnificat: He has brought down the powerful from their thrones and lifted up the lowly; He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty (Luke 1:52–53).
Mary's song is not a political programme, but it is the logic of God's Kingdom. God is on the side of the lowly. A poor girl of Nazareth became the Mother of God.
This Christmas fast, let us save something: the money from a meal we skip, a luxury we give up, and give it to the poor. Then our fast will sing Mary's song. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary sang that God loves the poor. Share something with a poor child this Christmas!

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews warns: take care that none of you has an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God; exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today (Hebrews 3:12–13). The generation in the desert did not enter God's rest because of unbelief.
Notice the words every day and today. Faith is not a feeling we had once; it is renewed each day. And we need one another: exhort one another. A Christian alone is easily discouraged.
In the Gospel Jesus says: your eye is the lamp of your body; if your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light (Luke 11:34). What we look at shapes what we become.

What do our eyes feed on: screens full of violence, envy and impurity, or the Word of God and the beauty of creation? During this fast, guard your eyes, and encourage one person in their faith today. Amen.
kids: Children, your eyes are like windows. Let good things come in through them, and your heart will be full of light!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Corinthians to clean out the old yeast so that they may be a new batch, for Christ our paschal lamb has been sacrificed (1 Corinthians 5:7). Sin tolerated in a community spreads like yeast through dough.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches that each tree is known by its fruit: the good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good, for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks (Luke 6:45).
Today we remember St John of the Cross, the Carmelite mystic who taught that God purifies us in the dark night, taking away false supports so that we may love Him alone.
The fast is a time to clean out the old yeast: a bad habit, a grudge, a sinful relationship. Ask God to purify your heart, so that good fruit may come from it. Make a good confession this week. Amen.
kids: Children, a good tree gives good fruit. When your heart is good, your words and actions will be good too!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul writes: by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God (Ephesians 2:8). We were dead through our sins, and God, rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ.
Salvation is a gift, but it is not lazy. Paul adds that we are created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand for us to walk in (Ephesians 2:10).

In the Gospel John the Baptist appears in the wilderness preaching: repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near. He is the voice of one crying out: prepare the way of the Lord, make His paths straight (Matthew 3:2–3). And people came to confess their sins.
Let us prepare the way for Christ: straighten what is crooked, lower the mountains of pride, fill the valleys of neglect. A good confession is the best preparation for Christmas. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist told people to get ready for Jesus. Get your heart ready by saying sorry for your mistakes!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul thanks God that the Thessalonians received his preaching not as a human word, but as what it really is, God's word, which is at work in you believers (1 Thessalonians 2:13). The Word of God is not just information; it acts in us.
In the Gospel Jesus says: whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much (Luke 16:10).
Small things matter: honesty in a small payment, faithfulness in daily prayer, keeping a small promise. These build a character that God can trust with great things.

Jesus also says: no slave can serve two masters; you cannot serve God and wealth (Luke 16:13). During this fast, let us examine our money and our hearts. Who is our master? Let us be faithful in little things this week. Amen.
kids: Children, being honest in small things makes Jesus very happy. Tell the truth even when it is hard!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul writes: in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith; as many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:26–27). There is no longer Jew or Greek, slave or free, male and female; all are one in Christ.

In the Gospel Zechariah, filled with the Holy Spirit, sings: blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for He has looked favourably on His people and redeemed them (Luke 1:68). His long silence ends in praise.

He sings to his little son: you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare His ways, to give knowledge of salvation by the forgiveness of sins (Luke 1:76–77).
And he ends: by the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us (Luke 1:78). Christmas is near. Let us pray the Benedictus this week and get ready for the dawn. Amen.
kids: Children, Zechariah sang a beautiful song when John was born. Sing a song of thanks to God today!

homily: Dear friends, today our Church remembers the Miraculous Cross at Mylapore, the ancient stone cross connected with the memory of the apostle Thomas. It reminds us that our faith in India is very old, and that it is a faith in the Cross of Christ.
In the desert, when the people were dying of thirst, Moses struck the rock and water came out (Exodus 17:6). The Fathers saw in this rock the pierced side of Christ, from which flow the sacraments.

St Paul writes that Christ is our peace: through the Cross He broke down the dividing wall of hostility and made us one people (Ephesians 2:14–16). And in the Gospel Jesus tells Thomas: I am the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14:6).
Let us venerate the Cross with love today. Let us ask the Crucified One to break down walls of hostility in our families and our Church, and to keep us on the Way that Thomas preached. Amen.
kids: Children, the cross shows us how much Jesus loves us. Make the sign of the cross slowly and with love today!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells how God set him apart before he was born and called him through grace, and was pleased to reveal His Son to him (Galatians 1:15–16). Like Jeremiah and John the Baptist, Paul was called from the womb.
Each of us too was known and called by God before birth. Our life is not an accident. Christmas, the birth of the Son, reminds us of the dignity of every birth.
In the Gospel John the Baptist says of Jesus: the one who comes from above is above all; He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for He gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:31–34).

Let us thank God today for our own life and vocation, and pray for unborn children and for mothers awaiting birth this Christmas. And let us listen to the words of Christ, who gives the Spirit without measure. Amen.
kids: Children, God knew you even before you were born, and He loves you very much. Thank Him for your life today!

homily: Dear friends, four days before Christmas the Church reads the opening of John's Gospel: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; all things came into being through Him (John 1:1–3).

Before Bethlehem there is eternity. The Child in the manger is the eternal Word through whom the universe was made. That is why Christmas is not just a sweet story, but the greatest mystery: the Creator becomes a creature.
John adds: in Him was life, and the life was the light of all people; the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it (John 1:4–5).

St Paul tells us to pray at all times in the Spirit (Ephesians 6:18). In these last days, let us pray more: a short visit to church, a family prayer at the crib, the Rosary. Let the Light find our hearts awake. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is the light of the world. When you light the star or lamp this Christmas, remember that Jesus is the true Light!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul gives the shortest Christmas creed: when the fullness of time had come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children (Galatians 4:4–5).
Because we are children, God has sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying Abba, Father! So you are no longer a slave but a child, and if a child then also an heir (Galatians 4:6–7).

In the Gospel John the Baptist came as a witness to testify to the light. The true light was coming into the world. He came to what was His own, and His own people did not accept Him. But to all who received Him, He gave power to become children of God (John 1:7–12).
The question of Christmas is simple: will we receive Him? Let us make room in our homes, our time and our hearts. Then we will be children of God, not only in name but in truth. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus came so that we could be God's children. When you pray Our Father, remember that God is your Father!

homily: Dear friends, two days before Christmas the whole Church waits. Isaiah gives names for the Child: Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6).

These names answer our needs. Are you confused? He is the Wonderful Counsellor. Are you weak? He is the Mighty God. Do you feel abandoned? He is the Everlasting Father. Is there conflict in your home? He is the Prince of Peace.
The long season of Annunciation, to Zechariah, to Mary, to Joseph, is ending. God has kept every promise. Now He asks only one thing: a place to be born.
In these last two days, prepare a place. Clean your heart in confession, reconcile with someone, and prepare the crib at home with your children. The Prince of Peace is coming. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is called the Prince of Peace. Make peace with your brother or sister today to get ready for Christmas!

homily: Dear friends, on Christmas Eve the Church looks to Bethlehem. Micah says: you, Bethlehem, one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth one who is to rule in Israel (Micah 5:2). God chooses the small.
A little town, a poor couple, a manger, shepherds in the fields: God's greatest work is done in the smallest places. No one is too small or too poor for Christ to come to them.
Bethlehem means house of bread. There the Bread of Life is born. Tonight, in the Holy Qurbana of the Nativity, He comes again under the appearance of bread.

Tonight families gather, stars are lit, carols are sung. Let us also keep a moment of silence before the crib, to adore the Child. Let us forgive one another, and welcome Him with simple hearts. A blessed Christmas to you all. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight baby Jesus is born! Kneel at the crib and tell Him: Jesus, I love you.

homily: Dear friends, at twelve years old Jesus stays behind in the Temple. Mary and Joseph search for Him for three days in anguish. When they find Him, He says: why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house? (Luke 2:49).

Even as a boy Jesus knows who His Father is. His first words in the Gospel speak of the Father. And yet He goes down to Nazareth and is obedient to Mary and Joseph (Luke 2:51). Obedience at home is part of His holiness.
St Paul writes: bear one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ; let us not grow weary in doing what is right (Galatians 6:2, 9). A family is a place where burdens are shared.

Parents, if your child seems lost, in faith or in life, keep searching with love and prayer, as Mary and Joseph did. Children, obey your parents as Jesus did. And all of us, let us bear one another's burdens this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus obeyed Mary and Joseph at home. Help your parents today without complaining!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul had a thorn in the flesh and begged the Lord three times to take it away. The answer came: my grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness (2 Corinthians 12:7–9).

Paul learned to accept his weakness, so that the power of Christ might dwell in him. Many of us carry thorns: illness, a difficult family situation, a weakness we cannot overcome. God's grace is enough.
In the Gospel the disciples are rowing across the sea at night in a strong wind. They see Jesus walking on the water and are terrified. He says: it is I; do not be afraid (John 6:19–20).
As the year ends, let us bring our fears and weaknesses to Jesus. He comes to us across the dark waters and says: it is I, do not be afraid. Amen.
kids: Children, when you are scared, remember Jesus says: it is I, do not be afraid. He is always near you!

homily: Dear friends, on the last day of the year the Church gives us a parable of mercy and urgency. A fig tree has borne no fruit for three years, and the owner says: cut it down. But the gardener pleads: sir, let it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and put manure on it; if it bears fruit next year, well and good (Luke 13:7–9).
Each new year is a gift of that patient gardener. God gives us one more year to bear fruit. He does not give up on us.
St Paul tells Timothy: there is great gain in godliness combined with contentment; fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of eternal life (1 Timothy 6:6, 12).

Tonight let us thank God for this year, ask pardon for our sins, and decide what fruit we want to bear next year: more prayer, more charity, a healed relationship. Let us begin the new year with the Holy Qurbana and with God. Amen.
kids: Children, God gives you a whole new year! Thank Him for this year and ask Him to help you grow good next year.

intro: Theme: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
The Annunciation to Mary, contrasted with Balaam who could not see the angel; Isaiah's promise of the Spirit fulfilled in Nazareth.

sub: Balaam does not see the angel; his donkey does.
Only when God opens his eyes does he bow down.
We too can be busy and blind before God.
q: Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road, with his drawn sword in his hand; and he bowed down, falling on his face.
And he came to her and said, “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you.”
points.apply: Ask God each morning to open your eyes to his presence.

sub: Isaiah promises the Spirit on Israel's descendants.
At Nazareth the Spirit overshadows Mary.
The Son of the Most High takes flesh.
q: For I will pour water on the thirsty land, and streams on the dry ground; I will pour my spirit upon your descendants, and my blessing on your offspring.
The angel said to her, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be holy; he will be called Son of God.”
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit daily until Christmas.

points.h: Here am I, the servant of the Lord
sub: Balaam obeys reluctantly; Mary consents freely.
Her yes is the model of faith.
Nothing is impossible with God.
q: Balaam said to Balak, “I have come to you now, but do I have power to say just anything? The word God puts in my mouth, that is what I must say.”
Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
points.apply: Say yes today to one thing God asks of you.

concl: Mary's yes opened the door to the Word.
Let our yes open our hearts to Christ this Christmas.
2026-12-06.resolve: Pray the Angelus at noon every day until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “His name is John: God has been gracious.”
The birth of John the Baptist, prepared by the promises to Abraham and the birth of Samson.

sub: Abraham welcomes three visitors and hears the promise of a son.
God's word is faithful across centuries.
Hospitality opens the door to blessing.
q: Then one said, “I will surely return to you in due season, and your wife Sarah shall have a son.” And Sarah was listening at the tent entrance behind him.
Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son. Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown his great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.
points.apply: Welcome a guest or stranger with generosity this week.

sub: Samson is a nazirite from birth.
John is filled with the Spirit from his mother's womb.
Every vocation begins in God's plan before birth.
q: For you shall conceive and bear a son. No razor is to come on his head, for the boy shall be a nazirite to God from birth. It is he who shall begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines.
All who heard them pondered them and said, “What then will this child become?” For, indeed, the hand of the Lord was with him.
points.apply: Bless your children each night this week.

sub: Zechariah obeys and writes the name.
His mouth is opened and he praises God.
Obedience leads to praise.
q: The LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And all of them were amazed. Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, praising God.
points.apply: End each day's silence with a prayer of praise.

concl: God is gracious; that is the meaning of this season.
Let us bless our children and praise the Lord.
2026-12-13.resolve: Pray the Benedictus (Luke 1:68–79) each morning until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “He did as the angel of the Lord commanded.”
The annunciation to Joseph; God's will discovered in families, from Rebekah and Hannah to Nazareth.

points.h: God's will in marriages and families
sub: Rebekah says “I will” and becomes Isaac's wife.
God guides families through prayer and trust.
Christmas begins in a home.
q: And they called Rebekah, and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” She said, “I will.”
Her husband Joseph, being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, planned to dismiss her quietly.
points.apply: Pray together as a couple or family for God's will this week.

sub: Hannah pours out her soul before the Lord.
God hears and gives Samuel.
Honest prayer opens the way for God's gift.
q: But Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman deeply troubled; I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.”

But just when he had resolved to do this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.”
points.apply: Tell God honestly what troubles you.

sub: Joseph names the child Jesus: “the Lord saves”.
He wakes and obeys at once.
Fathers learn from Joseph's silent courage.
q: He who finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favor from the LORD.
When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife.
points.apply: Pray to St Joseph for the fathers in your family.

concl: Joseph took Mary and Jesus into his home.
Let us do the same this Christmas.
2026-12-20.resolve: Pray to St Joseph every day until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “To you is born this day a Saviour.”
Christmas: the Word made flesh, born in Bethlehem, announced to shepherds, laid in a manger, the Bread of Life.

sub: The prophets promised Immanuel and the Prince of Peace.
In the fullness of time God sent his Son, born of a woman.
The child in the manger is the eternal Son.
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

But the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid; for see—I am bringing you good news of great joy for all the people: to you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is the Messiah, the Lord.”
points.apply: Kneel before the crib with your family and pray together.

points.h: Good news for the little ones
sub: Little Bethlehem, poor shepherds, a manger.
God comes in humility to all.
The sign is a child wrapped in cloths.
q: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origin is from of old, from ancient days.
This will be a sign for you: you will find a child wrapped in bands of cloth and lying in a manger.
points.apply: Share a Christmas meal or gift with a poor family.

points.h: Glory to God, peace on earth
sub: Heaven sings; earth receives peace.
The shepherds glorify God; Mary ponders.
Christmas must change our relationships.
q: They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
“Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favors!”
points.apply: Reconcile with someone today.

concl: The Bread of Life lies in the manger and on our altar.
Let us adore, ponder, and share the good news.
2026-12-25.resolve: Keep the twelve days of Christmas with daily prayer before the crib.

intro: Theme: “Jesus, Mary and Joseph, bless our family.”
The Holy Family in danger, exile and Nazareth; God's design for the family; honour for parents.

sub: Man and woman created in God's image.
Blessed to be fruitful.
The family is God's work before it is ours.
q: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them. God blessed them, and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply.”
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
points.apply: Thank God together for each member of your family.

sub: The fourth commandment carries a promise.
Care for parents in old age is holy.
Respect builds a home.
q: Those who honor their father atone for sins, and those who respect their mother are like those who lay up treasure.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
points.apply: Visit or call your elderly parents or grandparents.

sub: Warned in a dream, Joseph flees by night.
The Holy Family become refugees.
God protects them; they return to Nazareth.
q: When the child grew up, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and she took him as her son. She named him Moses, “because,” she said, “I drew him out of the water.”

Now after they had left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and remain there until I tell you; for Herod is about to search for the child, to destroy him.”
points.apply: Pray for migrant families and refugees.

concl: Holiness grows in ordinary family life lived with God.
Jesus, Mary and Joseph, protect our homes.
2026-12-27.resolve: Begin or renew daily family prayer.

intro: Theme: “Wake up, and be silent before the Word.”
Paul calls us to wake; Zechariah's doubt becomes a fruitful silence.

sub: Malachi promised a messenger before the Lord.
Gabriel announces that messenger: John.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
The angel replied, “I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.”
points.apply: Listen today for a message God may be sending.

sub: Zechariah asks for proof.
Silence becomes his school of faith.
q: Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?
Zechariah said to the angel, “How will I know that this is so? For I am an old man, and my wife is getting on in years.”
points.apply: Choose one daily silence during the fast.

sub: Salvation is nearer than when we first believed.
Put on the Lord Jesus Christ.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.
Because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time, you will become mute, unable to speak, until the day these things occur.
points.apply: Lay aside one “work of darkness” today.

concl: Salvation is near; wake up.
Let silence prepare us for praise.
2026-12-01.resolve: Keep a daily hour of silence during the 25 Days' Fast.

intro: Theme: “The faithful God and the One he sends.”
God is faithful; Jesus, sent by the Father, always does what pleases him.

sub: God's love is everlasting.
He calls us into fellowship with his Son.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
I have much to say about you and much to condemn; but the one who sent me is true, and I declare to the world what I have heard from him.
points.apply: Thank God for his faithfulness this year.

sub: When the Son of Man is lifted up, we will know “I am he”.
The Cross reveals who Jesus is.
q: You are my witnesses, says the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he.
So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but I speak these things as the Father instructed me.”
points.apply: Spend a moment before the crucifix today.

sub: The Father is always with the Son.
Doing his will, we are never alone.
q: Do not fear, for I am with you.
And the one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.
points.apply: Before each decision ask: does this please the Father?

concl: God is faithful to his promises.
The One sent is coming; we are never alone.
2026-12-02.resolve: Pray each morning: “Father, today I want to please you.”

intro: Theme: “Go into all the world.”
St Francis Xavier, apostle of the southern coast of India and patron of missions.

points.h: A people holy to the Lord
sub: God declares Israel his treasured people.
The baptised are called to holiness and mission.
q: Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people, as he promised you, and to keep his commandments.
He called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal call to holiness.

points.h: Turn to me and be saved
sub: Salvation is offered to all the ends of the earth.
Xavier went to the farthest ends he could reach.
q: Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.”
points.apply: Pray for missionaries from Kerala.

sub: The Servant is a light to the nations.
Every Christian shares this mission.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent.
points.apply: Share your faith with one person this week.

concl: Xavier was poor, yet made many rich.
The Gospel must be announced to all.
2026-12-03.resolve: Support a mission diocese or missionary this season.

intro: Theme: “Blessed are your eyes.”
Seek the things above; we see what the prophets longed to see. First Friday: the Sacred Heart.

points.h: The people who walked in darkness
sub: The prophets longed for the light.
The light has come in Christ.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in a land of deep darkness—on them light has shined.
But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.
points.apply: Thank God for the gift of faith.

sub: Many righteous people waited and did not see.
We stand at the threshold of the Incarnation.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it.
points.apply: Visit the Blessed Sacrament today.

sub: Raised with Christ, we seek heaven.
The Sacred Heart draws our hearts upward.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Consecrate your family to the Sacred Heart.

concl: We are blessed to see Christ.
Let us set our hearts on him.
2026-12-04.resolve: Fast from one kind of screen content during the 25 days.

intro: Theme: “Hand on the plough.”
Faith receives the Spirit; discipleship does not look back.

sub: Abraham believed and was reckoned righteous.
Believers share his blessing.
q: And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
points.apply: Make an act of faith today.

sub: Elisha left everything to follow Elijah.
A real decision has no way back.
q: He returned from following him, took the yoke of oxen, and slaughtered them; using the equipment from the oxen, he boiled their flesh, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out and followed Elijah, and became his servant.
Jesus said to him, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
points.apply: Give up one thing that pulls you back.

sub: Excuses delay discipleship.
Mary said yes at once.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?
Then he said to them all, “If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.”
points.apply: Pray the Rosary with Mary today.

concl: The Lord who comes asks for an undivided heart.
Let us follow without looking back.
2026-12-05.resolve: Renew your commitment to Christ at the Qurbana tomorrow.

intro: Theme: “Grow up into Christ.”
Maturity in faith and confident prayer; St Ambrose.

points.h: Call to me and I will answer
sub: God invites his people to call on him.
Jesus promises to act when we ask in his name.
q: Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things that you have not known.
I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If in my name you ask me for anything, I will do it.
points.apply: Bring one intention to Jesus with confidence.

sub: Believers continue Christ's works.
The Church's saints and missionaries prove it.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?
Very truly, I tell you, the one who believes in me will also do the works that I do and, in fact, will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.
points.apply: Do one work of mercy today in Jesus' name.

sub: Mature faith is not tossed about by every teaching.
Ambrose stood firm in truth and love.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if you do not, then believe me because of the works themselves.
points.apply: Read one page of the Catechism this week.

concl: Grow up into Christ.
Ask in his name, and do his works.
2026-12-07.resolve: Pray “in the name of Jesus” with faith each day this week.

intro: Theme: “The Mighty One has done great things for me.”
The Immaculate Conception: God prepared a pure dwelling for his Son, and Mary sings his mercy.

sub: After the Fall God promised enmity between the serpent and the woman.
Mary is the woman in whom the serpent had no share.
She was preserved from original sin in view of Christ's merits.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
And he came to her and said, “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you.”
points.apply: Thank God for Mary's victory over sin in Christ.

sub: Wisdom seeks a place to pitch its tent.
Isaiah's sign: the young woman bears Immanuel.
God prepared a pure home for his Son.
q: Then the Creator of all things gave me a command, and my Creator chose the place for my tent. He said, ‘Make your dwelling in Jacob, and in Israel receive your inheritance.’
Long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son.
points.apply: Prepare a clean heart through confession before Christmas.

sub: Mary's greatness is God's gift.
The Magnificat: humility and gratitude.
What God did in Mary he wants to complete in us.
q: I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness.
For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name. His mercy is for those who fear him from generation to generation.
points.apply: Pray the Magnificat each evening this week.

concl: God prepared Mary for Christ; he prepares us too.
Holy Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us.
2026-12-08.resolve: Make a good confession before Christmas.

intro: Theme: “Nothing will be impossible with God.”
Chosen in Christ; Mary's question and consent.

points.h: Chosen before the foundation of the world
sub: God's plan is eternal.
Each vocation is part of it.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you.
Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, since I am a virgin?”
points.apply: Thank God for your vocation.

points.h: The power of the Most High
sub: The Spirit overshadows Mary.
God's power accomplishes what nature cannot.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?
For nothing will be impossible with God.
points.apply: Give God one impossible situation today.

sub: Mary gives herself completely.
Her yes is free and total.
q: And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
points.apply: Say “Here I am, Lord” at the start of each day.

concl: God's plan is greater than our limits.
Let us answer with Mary: here I am.
2026-12-09.resolve: Pray the Angelus at noon this week.

intro: Theme: “Blessed is she who believed.”
The Visitation: faith becomes charity; Mary carries Christ to Elizabeth.

sub: The ark of the covenant brought blessing to Obed-edom's house for three months.
Mary, carrying Christ, stays three months with Elizabeth.
q: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months; and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.
In those days Mary set out and went with haste to a Judean town in the hill country.
points.apply: Bring Christ's blessing to one home this week.

sub: John leaps for joy before he is born.
Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit.
q: The LORD, your God, is in your midst, a warrior who gives victory.
For as soon as I heard the sound of your greeting, the child in my womb leaped for joy.
points.apply: Share your joy in Christ with someone today.

sub: Elizabeth praises Mary's faith.
Our blessing too is in believing God's word.
q: O daughter, you are blessed by the Most High God above all other women on earth.
And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
points.apply: Visit an elderly or lonely relative this week.

concl: Faith that receives Christ carries him to others.
Let us visit, serve and rejoice.
2026-12-10.resolve: Make one visit of charity before Christmas.

intro: Theme: “He has filled the hungry with good things.”
The Magnificat's reversal and Paul's call to fair sharing.

sub: Hannah sang it before Mary.
God's kingdom reverses human values.
q: He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap.
He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things.
points.apply: Do one act of respect for someone overlooked.

sub: In the desert manna was shared fairly.
Paul applies this to Christian giving.
q: But when they measured it with an omer, those who gathered much had nothing over, and those who gathered little had no shortage; they gathered as much as each of them needed.
He has helped his servant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy, according to the promise he made to our ancestors, to Abraham and to his descendants forever.
points.apply: Give what you save by fasting to the poor.

points.h: His mercy from generation to generation
sub: God's mercy is faithful through history.
Mary's song is the Church's song.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
His mercy is for those who fear him from generation to generation.
points.apply: Pray the Magnificat this evening.

concl: God's mercy lifts the lowly and feeds the hungry.
Our fasting should do the same.
2026-12-11.resolve: Give the savings of the 25 Days' Fast to a family in need.

intro: Theme: “Today, if you hear his voice.”
Do not harden your heart; let the eye be a lamp full of light.

sub: Israel hardened its heart in the desert.
Today is the day to listen.
q: O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness.
As it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”
points.apply: Listen to God in five minutes of silence today.

sub: Faith is sustained in community.
Encouragement protects against sin's deceit.
q: Two are better than one… For if they fall, one will lift up the other.
But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called “today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
points.apply: Encourage a friend in faith today.

sub: What we look at shapes us.
Christ's light must fill us before Christmas.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.

Your eye is the lamp of your body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light; but if it is not healthy, your body is full of darkness. Therefore consider whether the light in you is not darkness.
points.apply: Choose wholesome content today.

concl: Today is the day to listen.
Let Christ's light fill us.
2026-12-12.resolve: Fast from harmful content until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “Out of the abundance of the heart.”
A good tree, a clean heart; St John of the Cross.

sub: God promises to replace the heart of stone.
Conversion is God's work in us.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
No good tree bears bad fruit, nor again does a bad tree bear good fruit; for each tree is known by its own fruit.
points.apply: Ask God for a new heart in prayer today.

sub: Life flows from the heart.
Our words show what we store.
q: Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.
The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good, and the evil person out of evil treasure produces evil; for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.
points.apply: Replace one harsh word with a kind one today.

sub: The one who trusts God is like a tree by the stream.
St John of the Cross: God alone satisfies.
q: Blessed are those who trust in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD. They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream.
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Christmas.

concl: A good heart bears good fruit.
Let God purify and fill it.
2026-12-14.resolve: Examine your words each night this week.

intro: Theme: “Prepare the way of the Lord.”
Saved by grace; called to repentance by John.

sub: Isaiah announced a highway for God.
John is that voice.
q: A voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
In those days John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness of Judea, proclaiming, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
points.apply: Make your Christmas confession this week.

sub: Pride must be humbled, despair lifted.
Confession levels the road.
q: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill be made low; the uneven ground shall become level, and the rough places a plain. Then the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all people shall see it together.
This is the one of whom the prophet Isaiah spoke when he said, “The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.’”
points.apply: Settle one crooked matter this week.

sub: God gives a new heart and spirit.
Grace makes conversion possible.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you.
For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.
points.apply: Thank God for his mercy tonight.

concl: Grace comes first; repentance opens the door.
Prepare the way of the Lord.

intro: Theme: “One master.”
God's word at work; faithfulness in little; God, not wealth.

points.h: The word at work in you
sub: The Thessalonians received God's word as God's word.
It works in believers.
q: If I say, “I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,” then within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones.
Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
points.apply: Read Luke 2:1–20 slowly this week.

sub: God sees our small dealings.
Christmas spending tests our honesty and generosity.
q: Honor the LORD with your substance and with the first fruits of all your produce.
If then you have not been faithful with the dishonest wealth, who will entrust to you the true riches?
points.apply: Give generously to the poor this Christmas.

sub: An undivided heart serves one master.
The Child in the manger chose poverty.
q: Hear, O Israel: The LORD is our God, the LORD alone.
No slave can serve two masters; for a slave will either hate the one and love the other, or be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
points.apply: Spend less on yourself this Christmas.

concl: Let God's word rule our hearts this Christmas.
Serve one Master.
2026-12-16.resolve: Plan a simple, generous Christmas as a family.

intro: Theme: “The dawn from on high.”
Zechariah's Benedictus and our baptismal inheritance.

points.h: He has raised up a mighty saviour
sub: God remembers his covenant with David.
The promise is fulfilled in Jesus.
q: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me; your throne shall be established forever.
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them. He has raised up a mighty savior for us in the house of his servant David.
points.apply: Pray the Benedictus each morning.

sub: John prepares the Lord's way.
He gives knowledge of salvation by forgiveness.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me.
And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways, to give knowledge of salvation to his people by the forgiveness of their sins.
points.apply: Go to confession before Christmas.

sub: Isaiah saw a great light.
Christ is the dawn from on high.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in a land of deep darkness—on them light has shined.
By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
points.apply: Make peace with one person before Christmas.

concl: God has visited his people.
Let the dawn of Christ shine on us.
2026-12-17.resolve: Pray the Benedictus at sunrise until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “Peace through the Cross.”
The Miraculous Cross at Mylapore and the meaning of the Cross.

sub: Moses strikes the rock at Horeb.
From Christ's pierced side flow blood and water.
q: I will be standing there in front of you on the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people may drink.
Let the entire house of Israel know with certainty that God has made him both Lord and Messiah, this Jesus whom you crucified.
points.apply: Pray before the cross at home tonight.

sub: The bronze serpent lifted up brought healing.
The Cross lifted up brings salvation.
q: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
points.apply: Look at a crucifix in silence for five minutes.

sub: Thomas asks the way; Jesus is the way.
The St Thomas Christians honoured the Cross as the sign of life.
q: Do not fear, for I am with you.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
points.apply: Reconcile with one person before Christmas.

concl: The Cross of Christ is our peace and our way.
We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you.
2026-12-18.resolve: Teach your children the meaning of the cross in your home.

intro: Theme: “The One who comes from above.”
Paul called from the womb; John's witness to the One from heaven.

sub: Jeremiah, John and Paul were called from the womb.
Each of us has a vocation from God.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you.
The one who comes from above is above all; the one who is of the earth belongs to the earth and speaks about earthly things. The one who comes from heaven is above all.
points.apply: Thank God for your vocation today.

points.h: He speaks the words of God
sub: Jesus reveals the Father.
The Spirit is given without measure.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.
He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit before reading the Gospel.

sub: The Father has given all to the Son.
Believing in him is eternal life.
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders.
The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands.
points.apply: Set up the crib at home this weekend.

concl: The One from above is coming.
Let him be above all in our lives.
2026-12-19.resolve: Prepare the crib and pray before it each evening until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “The light shines in the darkness.”
The Prologue of John: the eternal Word who comes as a child.

sub: God created by his Word.
The Word is God from eternity.
q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
points.apply: Read John 1:1–14 slowly today.

sub: In the Word is life.
His light enlightens every person.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.
In him was life, and the life was the light of all people. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
points.apply: Bring one dark situation into Christ's light in prayer.

sub: The Son is begotten, not made.
At Christmas he is born in time.
q: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.”
All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being.
points.apply: Pray the Creed slowly, pausing at “begotten, not made”.

concl: The Word through whom all was made is coming as a child.
Let his light shine in us.
2026-12-21.resolve: Read the Prologue each day until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “Children of God.”
The Son born of a woman makes us God's children; to receive him is to become one.

sub: The Son takes flesh from Mary.
God enters history at the chosen time.
q: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law.
points.apply: Thank Mary for giving Jesus to the world.

sub: The Spirit makes us cry “Abba”.
We are heirs, not slaves.
q: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.”
And because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba! Father!” So you are no longer a slave but a child, and if a child then also an heir, through God.
points.apply: Pray the Our Father slowly today.

sub: His own did not accept him.
Those who receive him become God's children.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God.
points.apply: Make room for Christ through confession.

concl: The Son became a child of Mary so that we might become children of God.
Let us receive him.
2026-12-22.resolve: Prepare a place for Jesus: confession before Christmas.

intro: Theme: “A child has been born for us.”
Isaiah's names for the Messiah on the eve of Christmas Eve. (The day's official readings are pending.)

sub: Christ guides us in confusion.
His word is a lamp.
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
points.apply: Bring one confusing situation to Jesus in prayer.

sub: His reign brings endless peace.
He breaks down walls of hostility.
q: His authority shall grow continually, and there shall be endless peace for the throne of David and his kingdom.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives.
points.apply: Reconcile with someone before Christmas Eve.

sub: There was no room in the inn.
Make room in heart and home.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come.
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him.
points.apply: Pray before the crib tonight.

concl: The Child is almost here.
Let us make room for him.
2026-12-23.resolve: Finish the 25 Days' Fast with confession and charity.

intro: Theme: “O little Bethlehem.”
Christmas Eve: God chooses the small. (The day's official readings are pending.)

sub: Micah foretold the ruler from Bethlehem.
God chooses what is small.
q: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origin is from of old, from ancient days.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son and wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silence before the crib.

points.h: He shall be the one of peace
sub: The ruler from Bethlehem is a shepherd.
He is our peace.
q: And he shall stand and feed his flock in the strength of the LORD… and he shall be the one of peace.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
points.apply: Call someone who will be alone this Christmas.

sub: Bethlehem means house of bread.
The Bread of Life is born for us.
q: O taste and see that the LORD is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry.”
points.apply: Receive Communion at the Christmas Qurbana with deep faith.

concl: God comes in the small and the poor.
Let us adore him in silence.

intro: Theme: “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
St Stephen, the first martyr, the day after Christmas.

sub: Stephen sees the Son of Man at God's right hand.
Christ's birth opens heaven to us.
q: But they conspired against him, and by command of the king they stoned him to death in the court of the house of the LORD.
But filled with the Holy Spirit, he gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
points.apply: Pray for persecuted Christians.

sub: Jesus promised the Spirit would speak through his witnesses.
Stephen's wisdom could not be withstood.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh.
For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
points.apply: Ask the Spirit for courage to witness.

sub: Stephen commends his spirit and forgives.
Saul, watching, will become Paul.
q: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter.
While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
points.apply: Forgive someone today.

concl: The crib leads to the Cross and to heaven.
Let us forgive and witness like Stephen.
2026-12-26.resolve: Pray each day of the octave for one person who hurt you.

intro: Theme: “Rachel weeping for her children.”
The Holy Innocents and Holy Childhood Day.

sub: Abel's blood cries from the ground.
God is never deaf to the innocent.
q: And the LORD said, “What have you done? Listen; your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground!”
When Herod saw that he had been tricked by the wise men, he was infuriated, and he sent and killed all the children in and around Bethlehem who were two years old or under.
points.apply: Pray for children who suffer violence.

sub: Jeremiah's lament becomes the cry of Bethlehem.
God promises a future of hope.
q: Thus says the LORD: Keep your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for there is a reward for your work, says the LORD.
A voice was heard in Ramah, wailing and loud lamentation, Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be consoled, because they are no more.
points.apply: Console a mother who has lost a child.

sub: The Innocents' treasure is with God.
Children who share store up treasure in heaven.
q: But the righteous live forever, and their reward is with the Lord; the Most High takes care of them.
But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes and where thieves do not break in and steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Help children share a gift with poor children.

concl: God hears every innocent cry.
Let us protect and serve the little ones.
2026-12-28.resolve: Support a work for vulnerable children this season.

intro: Theme: “In my Father's house.”
The finding in the Temple and the law of mutual burden-bearing.

sub: Samuel grew in favour with God and people.
Jesus grew in wisdom and years.
q: Now the boy Samuel continued to grow both in stature and in favor with the LORD and with the people.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
points.apply: Pray for the growth of the children in your family.

sub: Jesus knows his true Father.
Mary and Joseph search in anguish and find him.
q: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not rely on your own insight.
He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
points.apply: Visit the church this week.

sub: The Son of God obeys at Nazareth.
Christian love carries others.
q: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them.
points.apply: Carry one burden for a family member.

concl: Jesus belongs to the Father and lives in a family.
Let us seek him and carry one another.
2026-12-29.resolve: Pray together as a family before the new year.

intro: Theme: “It is I; do not be afraid.”
Grace in weakness; Jesus walking on the sea.

sub: God parted the sea for Israel.
Jesus walks on the sea.
q: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The LORD drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night, and turned the sea into dry land; and the waters were divided.
When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were terrified.
points.apply: Name one storm and give it to Jesus.

sub: God hushes the waves.
Jesus' word calms our fear.
q: He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
But he said to them, “It is I; do not be afraid.”
points.apply: Pray “Jesus, I trust in you” when anxious.

sub: Paul's thorn remains; grace suffices.
Weakness becomes the place of Christ's power.
q: But those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength.
But he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.”
points.apply: Offer one weakness to God.

concl: The Lord of the storm is with us.
His grace is enough for the new year.
2026-12-30.resolve: Enter the new year with an act of trust.

intro: Theme: “One more year.”
Thanksgiving, repentance and resolve at the end of the year.

points.h: Bless the Lord, forget not his benefits
sub: Look back with gratitude.
God has crowned the year with his goodness.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits.
There is great gain in godliness combined with contentment.
points.apply: List ten blessings of the year and thank God.

sub: The fig tree has borne no fruit.
The gardener pleads for one more year.
q: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
He replied, ‘Sir, let it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and put manure on it. If it bears fruit next year, well and good; but if not, you can cut it down.’
points.apply: Make a good confession before the new year.

sub: Teach us to count our days.
Take hold of eternal life.
q: So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart.
Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called.
points.apply: Choose one fruit to bear in the new year.

concl: God's mercies are new every morning.
Let us begin the new year bearing fruit.
2026-12-31.resolve: Begin the new year with Holy Qurbana and a concrete resolution.
